en: The Apadāna of the Elder Sīvali Chapter on Bhaddiya, Number Three I was a king named Mahāsena, ruling over the earth with its oceans. At that time, the Buddha Kassapa, the peerless one among men, appeared in the world. Having heard of his arrival, I went forth from home into homelessness under him. There I practiced the holy life for twenty thousand years. Then, having passed away from there, I was reborn in the Brahmā world. From there, passing away, I was reborn in the city of Benares. “The Victor named Padumuttara,
the one with vision regarding all phenomena,
[appeared] one hundred thousand aeons hence.”
In that kappa, the Leader appeared.
His virtue was incalculable,
and his concentration was like a thunderbolt.
Incalculable is his supreme knowledge,
and his liberation is beyond compare—
among humans, gods, and nāgas.
In an assembly of Brahmins,
crowded with recluses and Brahmins,
the Leader taught the Dhamma.
He established as foremost among his disciples one who was a great gainer of wealth, possessed of merit,
and radiant with splendor.
Confident among the assemblies.
At that time, I was a kshatriya in the city called Haṃsa.
Having heard those words of the Victor concerning the many virtues of his disciple,
he invited him for seven days.
Having fed him along with his disciples and having given a great gift,
I aspired for that state.
Then, seeing me bowed at his feet, the Hero, that bull among men,
with a great voice, said:
He spoke these words:
"Then the great multitude, desiring to hear the word of the Conqueror,"
The devas, dānavas, and gandhabbas,
and the Brahmās of great psychic power;
as well as the ascetics and brahmins—
They paid homage with palms joined:
“Homage to you, O noble steed among men!
Homage to you, O supreme among men!”
A great gift was given by a khattiya for even seven days;
you who desire to hear its fruit—
“Give an explanation, O Great Sage.
Then the Blessed One said:
“Listen to my words;”
Established in the immeasurable Buddha and the Saṅgha,
who could possibly describe the extent of that merit?
For its fruit is immeasurable;
even if one possesses great wealth,
they aspire for the highest state.
"May I too become like the monk Sudassana,
who has obtained abundant gains."
In the future, after a hundred thousand eons,
you will be born into the family of Okkāka.
One named Gotama by clan will become a teacher in the world;
he will be an heir to his teachings.
“Born from the heart, fashioned by Dhamma,
he shall be a disciple of the Teacher, known by the name Sīvalī.”
By that well-performed kamma and by my intentions and aspirations,
having cast off this human body,
I went to the realm of the Thirty-three.
Ninety-one eons ago,
Vipassī was the Leader of the World.
One of beautiful appearance arose,
a seer of all phenomena.
At that time, in Bandhumatī, I—
And in a certain family,
beloved and esteemed,
I was occupied with my work.
At that time, a certain guild commissioned a refectory for the Great Seer Vipassī.
Greatly renowned and vast.
When the great almsgiving was completed,
they gave food consisting of various kinds of snacks.
They did not see fresh curd or honey at all; then,
having taken that [mixture], I...
Fresh curd and honey as well—
I went to the house of the master of the work,
and they found me and struck me.
Even after giving a thousand,
they did not obtain those two;
then I thought thus:
"This will not be insignificant,
since all these people pay such honor to the Tathāgata."
"I too shall perform service for the Leader of the World together with the Saṅgha.
Having thought thus, at that time, I—
Having mixed curd and honey together,
I offered it to the Lord of the World together with his Saṅgha.
By that well-performed kamma and by my intentions and aspirations,
having abandoned this human body,
I went to the realm of the Thirty-three.
Again, having been a king of great renown in Bārāṇasī, I—
Then, being malicious toward Sattuka,
I caused the gates to be blocked.
At that time, the ascetics were obstructed;
For one day I was protected;
then, as the result of that,
I fell into a terrible hell.
And now, in my final existence,
I was born in the city of the Koliyans;
Suppavāsā was my mother.
Mahāli was the Licchavi father.
By his kṣatriya merit and by the power of blocking the gates, [he attained this].
I dwelt for seven years,
suffering within my mother’s womb;
for seven days I was lost at the entrance.
Overwhelmed by great suffering,
my mother was thus deeply distressed because of her gift of consent.
I have set out from Suvatthi,
favored by the Buddha;
on the very day I departed,
I went forth into homelessness.
Sāriputta was my preceptor,
and Moggallāna was of great psychic power.
As he was shaving off my hair,
the Greatly Wise One instructed me;
while my hair was being cut, [he spoke].
I attained arahantship;
gods, nāgas, and humans bring me the requisites.
The Lord Padumuttara and the Guide Vipassī—
whomever I worshipped with joy,
Due to the specific distinction of their conditions,
the fruit of those karmas is most extensive and supreme.
I obtain gain everywhere—
in the forest and the village, on water and on land—
for the sake of seeing Revata.
When the Leader, the Guide of the World, departed together with thirty thousand bhikkhus.
Then, O Great-Minded One, for my sake, the Great Hero was provided with requisites brought by the gods.
The Leader of the World together with his Saṅgha was attended by me;
having gone there, I saw the Buddha at Revata.
Then, having gone to Jetavana,
he placed me among those foremost in this world:
"Sīvalī is the foremost of those who receive offerings."
"Among my disciples, O monks," the Teacher, who seeks the welfare of the entire world,
has praised me before his assemblies.
The defilements have been burnt away by me;
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me...
[and so forth] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable Elder Sīvali speak these verses.
This is the third *apadāna* of the Elder Sīvali.
